techniques_used.key_result: Hexagonal BN phase confirmed by peaks at 26.8°, 41.7°, 43.8°, 49.9°, 54.9°, 75.8°, and 82.1°; Cu peaks at 43.3° and 50.2° for (111) and (200) facets
techniques_used.source_quote: The characteristic peaks could be seen at 26.8°, 41.7°, 43.8°, 49.9°, 54.9°, 75.8°, and 82.1°, which could be assigned to the hexagonal phase of BN... another two diffraction peaks at 43.3° and 50.2° appeared over Cu/BN-NS and Cu/BN-NF, which could be attributed to the (111) and (200) facets of metallic Cu
The specific surface areas of BN-NS, BN-NF, and BN-NP were 4.6–13.2 m2 g−1

techniques_used.key_result: Cu particle sizes: 12.7 nm (Cu/BN-NS), 9.7 nm (Cu/BN-NF), 7.4 nm (Cu/BN-NP)
techniques_used.source_quote: The average sizes of Cu nanoparticles on the three catalysts were analyzed, and they were 12.7, 9.7, and 7.4 nm on Cu/BN-NS, Cu/BN-NF, and Cu/BN-NP, respectively

techniques_used.key_result: B 1s at 190.2 eV (B-N), 192.6 eV (B-O-N); N 1s at 398.1 eV (B-N), 400.2 eV (B-O-N); Cu 2p3/2 at 932.8 eV
techniques_used.source_quote: The binding energies of B were located at 190.2 eV and 192.6 eV... The binding energies of N were centered at 398.1 eV and 400.2 eV... the peaks at 932.8 eV and 952.5 eV could be observed over the Cu 2p spectra

techniques_used.key_result: LSPR absorption peak at 550-600 nm for Cu/BN catalysts
techniques_used.source_quote: Obvious absorption peaks of Cu/BN-NS, Cu/BN-NF, and Cu/BN-NP in the range of 550–600 nm could be observed, which could be attributed to the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect of Cu-NPs

morphology.value: BN nanosheets (500-1000 nm), nanofibers (100-300 nm diameter), nanoparticles (~500 nm); Cu nanoparticles (7.4-12.7 nm) deposited on BN
morphology.source_quote: BN-NS had nanosheet morphologies with sizes varying in the range of 500–1,000 nm... BN-NF had nanofiber structures with 100–300 nm of diameter... BN-NP were of nanoparticle morphologies with an average particle size of around 500 nm... small dark spots were observed over the TEM images of the three Cu/BN catalysts... the dark spots were Cu-NPs

structure.value: Hexagonal BN phase confirmed; Cu nanoparticles with (111) and (200) facets observed
structure.source_quote: The characteristic peaks could be seen at 26.8°, 41.7°, 43.8°, 49.9°, 54.9°, 75.8°, and 82.1°, which could be assigned to the hexagonal phase of BN... another two diffraction peaks at 43.3° and 50.2° appeared over Cu/BN-NS and Cu/BN-NF, which could be attributed to the (111) and (200) facets of metallic Cu

electronic_properties.value: Electron coupling between Cu-NPs and BN-NF observed via XPS peak shifts
electronic_properties.source_quote: Over the Cu/BN-NF catalyst, compared to the support BN-NF, the intensity of the peak attributed to B at 190.2 eV was shortened and the peak at 192.6 eV was sharpened... whereas the peak of N centered at 398.1 eV was bigger and the peak at 400.2 eV was smaller over Cu/BN-NF catalyst. It indicated the electron coupling between Cu-NPs and BN-NF

optical_properties.value: BN absorbs <400 nm; Cu/BN shows LSPR absorption at 550-600 nm extending to NIR
optical_properties.source_quote: The light absorption edge of three pristine BN supports was mainly located at UV light range with a wavelength shorter than 400 nm... After the loading of Cu, the light absorption capacities of Cu/BN catalysts were extended to visible light and even near-infrared light regions... Obvious absorption peaks of Cu/BN-NS, Cu/BN-NF, and Cu/BN-NP in the range of 550–600 nm could be observed

surface_properties.value: Pore sizes mainly 2-10 nm and 20-100 nm; III-type adsorption isotherms
surface_properties.source_quote: Their pore sizes were mainly distributed in the range of 2–10 and 20–100 nm... all three BN supports adsorption-desorption isotherms exhibited the properties of III-type of adsorption-desorption isotherms
